title: Diary of the Last Gravedigger
text: "Day 42. I have ceased counting coffins. The ground here is hard, and the dead insist on knocking from within. Yesterday I buried the blacksmith, Master Orlov. This morning he stood shivering upon my threshold, humbly requesting his boots. I informed him I had already traded them to the tavern keeper for mutton. He hung his hollow jaw and shuffled off into the mist. Now I dare not visit the tavern."

title: Treatise on Cold Iron and Bone
text: "The bone of a sinner hardens after death, but iron remains the only true ward against the restless. When forging a blade for the crypts, quench the steel not in well water, but in brine mixed with powdered saint-graves. The edge will bite through calcium and marrow alike, turning even ancient kings into brittle gravel."

title: Litany of the Hollow Monarch
text: "Before Morvath took the crown of bones, he was a just lord who wept for his dying soldiers. But justice does not stop the winter plague. When his daughter succumbed, he traded his heartbeat to the entities below the bedrock. Now his crown sits fused to his skull, and his tears have frozen into black glass."

title: The Ghoul's Palate
text: "An excerpt from an anonymous cultist's journal: 'Do not strike the ghoul while it feeds upon your fallen companion. It enters a state of near-religious ecstasy, blind to all worldly light. If you must strike, aim for the nape where the spine joins the bloated neck. If you miss, you become the second course.'"

title: Prioress Vespera's Confession
text: "My sisters believed the holy water would cleanse the necrosis spreading through the lower parish. They poured it into the wells until the font ran dry. But the water turned dark as bile in our goblets. Now my hands itch with thorns of silver, and when I pray, only the dead answer with wet, rasping sighs."

title: Ossuary Masonry: Volume I
text: "To raise an archway of human skulls, one must wedge the keystones with ground limestone and hardened sinew. A wall of bones breathes with the weather; in damp seasons it moans, in dry seasons it chatters. Lift with your thighs, novice, for stone is heavy, but the weight of unburied souls is heavier."

title: Eulogy for the Nameless Vanguard
text: "They marched down into the crypts with polished brass lanterns and shields bearing the white hawk. No herald recorded their names. Thirty years later, we found their armor standing upright against the wall, empty of flesh, polished immaculately by the scuttling beetles."

title: The Screaming Urn
text: "Never shatter an urn sealed with grey wax. The priests did not seal ashes within; they sealed the final screams of plague victims boiled alive in rosemary oil. Break the seal, and the vapor will blister your lungs before your knees find the floor."

title: Rune of the Skeletal Guard
text: "Watch the movement of the skeleton. It possesses neither muscle nor breath to telegraph its strike. It moves with the pure, economical geometry of lever and pivot. To evade the dead, one must not anticipate their eyes, but listen to the dry friction of their knee joints."

title: Fallen Paladin's Scrap
text: "My shield is dented beyond repair. Brother Justin turned two hours ago; his eyes burned with that sickly violet glow. I had to crush his throat with my pommel. God has abandoned this floor. If anyone finds this scrap, tell Brenda I kept her ribbon under my chainmail."

title: Anatomy of the Banshee
text: "The wail of the crypt banshee is not sound; it is a frequency of absolute grief that resonates directly with the calcium in your bones. Those who survive her shriek report that their teeth vibrate loose in their gums and the flame in their torches shrinks to a dying blue bead."

title: Tome of Marrow Transmutation
text: "Blood is fleeting and spills onto the flagstones to be lapped up by vermin. But the marrow hidden within the femurs holds the concentrated warmth of life. Crack the bone open upon an anvil, recite the Third Syllable of Vorash, and draw the vital warmth into your own veins."

title: Ballad of the Red Duke
text: "Ten verses detailing Duke Cassian, who walled himself inside his family vault with twelve cases of vintage wine, his finest hounds, and his personal jester. By day fifteen, only the hounds were singing. By day twenty, the jester was the Duke."

title: Notes on Tomb Moss
text: "The luminous moss that coats the sarcophagi tastes like bitter almonds and damp linen. Chewing it numbs toothache, but causes vivid dreams of drowning in cold tallow. Recommended only when rations run out completely."

title: The Scribe's Broken Quill
text: "I was ordered to catalogue the ancestral treasures of House Valerius. But there are no rubies here. There are only lead coffins soldered shut from the outside with warnings etched in three dead languages. Something is scratching at the lead from within. It has been scratching for two hundred years."

title: Malediction of the Tomb Robber
text: "He who takes the gold coin from the dead man's tongue must be swift as the adder. The dead strike not with fury, but with patience. Aim your dagger between the ribs where the shroud has rotted away, for there lies the brittle heart-cord."

title: Fragment: The First Burial
text: "They dug into the bedrock before the kingdom had a name. The elders said: 'The deeper the dead lie, the less they dream of the sun.' They were wrong. Depth only sharpens their envy of those who walk beneath the daylight."

title: Lament of the Gatekeeper
text: "The key to the lower crypt is made of brass and weighed seven pounds. I dropped it down the dry well because I could no longer endure the sound of the things pacing behind the threshold. Now the door is bowing outward under their combined weight."

title: Catalogue of Broken Crests
text: "Eighty shields recovered from the western crypt gallery. Each crest battered flat by morningstars. Yet the iron endures. True resilience is not born of gilded pride, but of scars borne in silence upon the breastplate."

title: Last Rites for the Condemned
text: "May the dirt sit heavy upon your breast. May the earthworms reject your flesh. May no candle be lit in your memory, lest you remember the shape of flame and seek to burn our roofs in your longing."

title: The Ratcatcher's Secret Recipes
text: "Vermin from the lower cisterns must be parboiled thrice in wild vinegar. Failure to do so will result in their tail twitching in your throat well after dinner. If the flesh glows emerald in the dark, rejoice—it saves on candle wax, and adds a zesty tang to stale hardtack."

title: Heretical Alchemy: Dissolving Flesh
text: "Mix two drams of vitriol with the distilled bile of an acid slime. Heat over charcoal until green vapors ascend. This solvent dissolves bone in seconds while leaving glass and lead untouched. Knowledge is the ultimate solvent; it dissolves morality faster than acid dissolves skin."

title: Ode to the Great Green Eye
text: "We cast our offal into the central drain, and the drain gazed back at us. A single yellow pupil, three paces wide, floating beneath the scum. It did not blink when we lowered the lantern. It smiled with eighty needle teeth, and we knelt in the foul water and wept with joy."

title: Journal of the Flesh-Stitcher
text: "The human forearm is sadly limited by its singular elbow joint. Today I grafted the knee of a trench hound to brother Barth's shoulder. He complained of the phantom barking for three days, but his reach with the halberd has improved by half a fathom."

title: Krazik's Gospel of the Gutter
text: "The surface men live in their towers of brittle stone, dreading the rain. But we who dwell in the run-off know that all their glory eventually washes down to our feet. Their perfumes, their crown jewels, their dead bastards—all belong to the gutter king at last."

title: Toxicity Tolerance Field Guide
text: "To survive the noxious vapors of the lower collectors, swallow a pinch of sulfur and dried marsh toad skin each morning. Your breath will curdle milk and dogs will howl at your passing, but your lungs will turn leathery as boiled shoe leather."

title: The Drowner's Lullaby
text: "Down in the culvert where shadows weep, / Green scum blankets the sinner's sleep. / Open your mouth and let in the tide, / For bloated things in the dark abide. / No bells will ring, no candles gleam, / Only the bubbles of your final dream."

title: Slime Husbandry for Ambitious Novices
text: "Acid slimes make poor watchdogs, as they are prone to dissolving their own kennels. However, if fed on a steady diet of rusted nails and criminal fingers, they produce a pungent slime that makes excellent axle grease for dungeon drawbridges."

title: Confessions of a City Sewer Engineer
text: "I warned the magistrate that the aqueduct connected directly to the pre-human vaults. He insisted on cutting costs. When the water in the public bathhouses turned red and began chanting in tongues, he had me arrested and thrown down the very drain I designed."

title: The Stalker's Camouflage
text: "Coat yourself in river silt and grease from dead eels. The eye of the surface dweller is drawn to shine and movement; break your silhouette against the slime-stained brick. Breathe through a hollow reed and strike only when their lantern flickers."

title: The Feast of the Murk Amalgam
text: "It does not chew. It simply folds its bulk over the unwary like a wet carpet made of rotting meat. Inside its gut, you remain alive for twenty minutes, listening to the murmurs of the three hundred men who were digested before you."

title: Warning: The Red Discharge
text: "If valve four begins leaking crimson foam, do not attempt to tighten the brass spigot with a wrench. The valve is no longer metal; it has developed teeth. Abandon the pump room immediately and bar the door with heavy timber."

title: Leech-Gatherer's Manual
text: "Abyssal leeches are twice the size of a man's thumb and possess three concentric rings of obsidian teeth. If one latches to your wrist, do not pull—it will rip the tendon. Apply a burning ember to its tail, and catch the extracted blood in a pewter cup. Drink it while warm."

title: Fever Dreams in the Sump
text: "Day 14 without sunlight. The dripping has formed a language. Four short drips, one long splatter. It translates to: 'She is coming down the pipe.' I put my ear to the drain grate and heard the rustle of wet silk."

title: The Bell of Heresy
text: "Cast from the melted crucifixes of seven sacked chapels, the bell rests in the flooded sanctuary of the sewer. When struck with a femur, its sound makes the listener believe their skin is covered in swarming fleas until they claw their own veins open."

title: Apothecary's Contraband Ledger
text: "Smuggled goods ledger: Three crates of powdered basilisk spleen, sixteen vials of blind mole-rat distillate, forty jars of black lotus tincture. The guards were paid in silver sovereigns dipped in sewer oil so they could not be spent without suspicion."

title: The Trench Hermit's Last Words
text: "You think you walk through sewage, young knight? You walk through the digestive tract of something slumbering beneath the continent. Every brick we laid is merely a parasite's egg clinging to its intestinal lining."

title: Mutagenic Salve Recipe
text: "Mix crushed sewer beetles, tallow from a drowned woman, and the bile of a giant rat. Rub into the skin before battle. The resulting hives will thicken into chiton plates within an hour, though the scratching will drive you mad by dusk."

title: The Rat King's Scepter
text: "It was not made of gold or silver, but of forty-eight living rats whose tails were knotted into an intricate spiral by dried blood. When the ratman holding it pointed, the horde moved like a single wave of black fur."

title: Drainage Worker's Strike Notice
text: "We refuse to enter Sector 9 until the management provides torches that cannot be extinguished by wet screams. Three men were dragged into the overflow pipe this week. We have our heavy iron pipe wrenches, and we know how to swing them."

title: The Smith's Soul-Pact
text: "To forge metal that never dulls, one must temper the blade in the screams of an unbaptized apprentice. Master Ignis traded his four sons to the pit demons for a crucible that burns with black flame. Now he stands at the anvil day and night, hammering out collars for beasts yet unborn."

title: Treatise on Basalt Smelting
text: "Common iron bends under the weight of a troll's club. True defense requires folding volcanic slag with crushed diamond dust under eight hundred blows of the steam hammer. The resulting plate is black as midnight, cold to the touch, and rejects all fire."

title: Ode to the Living Magma
text: "It flows like blood from the cracked belly of the mountain. It has no eyes, yet it seeks out the hollow places of the dungeon. When it cools, it traps the bones of giants in glassy amber. Respect the stone that melts, for you too are made of clay."

title: Diary of an Escaped Slave
text: "The taskmasters do not carry whips of leather; their whips are made of braided copper wire heated white-hot in the blast furnace. If you show weakness, they brand your back with the foundry sigil. I have crawled through the soot flues for three miles. My hair has burned away, but I can hear the cooler air above."

title: The Golem's Internal Architecture
text: "A golem of cast iron possesses no soul to bargain with, which makes it reliable. Inside its chest cavity sits a caged flame elemental driven mad by cold iron runes. Starve the fire, and the golem slows; feed it pitch and bones, and it crushes fortress gates like dry straw."

title: Vulkania's Brood Cycle
text: "Every hundred years, the magma wyrm lays seven eggs of solid obsidian in the deepest lava trenches. The hatchlings feed upon sulfur crystals and molten zinc until their scales turn harder than forged steel. Woe to the miners who dig into their nursery."

title: The Four Hammers of Ignis
text: "First hammer: Grief, which shapes the raw ingot. Second hammer: Wrath, which draws out the blade. Third hammer: Cruelty, which hardens the edge. Fourth hammer: Silence, which shatters the soul of the bearer when the work is complete."

title: Cinder Sprites: A Pestilence
text: "Do not leave dry rations near the forge vents. Ash imps crawl up the flue pipes like fiery spiders, defecating hot coals into your flour barrels and giggling with voices like crackling dry pine needles. Extinguish them with sand; water only makes them steam with laughter."

title: Pyromancer's Final Formula
text: "Fire is not an element; it is an appetite. To cast the true meteor, you must not invoke arcane words—you must surrender a portion of your own warmth to the void until your fingertips turn black with frost while your palms shoot roaring flame."

title: The Chained Titan of Forge Three
text: "He was taller than the pillars, with a beard of rusted iron filings. They bolted his wrists to the cavern floor with links as thick as oak trunks. His breath drives the giant bellows day and night. When he sighs, earthquakes shake the kingdoms above."

title: Operating Manual: The Soul Crucible
text: "Warning: Never open the viewing latch without amber glass goggles. The light of three thousand souls vaporizing under liquid brimstone will scorch your retinas permanently. If the molten bath turns purple, add two barrels of crushed saltpeter immediately."

title: Cooling Techniques for Heavy Sabatons
text: "When marching across magma crusts, line your boots with three layers of wool soaked in rendered lard and powdered talc. The fat will sizzle and smoke, but your soles will remain blister-free long enough to cross the slag lake."

title: The Iron Taskmaster's Brand
text: "The mark stamped upon the forehead of the foundry slaves is shaped like a cracked anvil. It burns with phantom heat whenever the master strikes his great hammer five miles away, reminding them that escape is an illusion."

title: The Slag Trench Mass Grave
text: "When the slaves die of heat exhaustion, their bodies are thrown directly into the slag runoff. Their bones burn away, but their teeth survive, floating like white pearls upon the glowing crimson surface of the waste channels."

title: Hymn to the Black Anvil
text: "Strike while the iron is pale! / Strike till the shadows quail! / The hammer does not weep for the ore, / The anvil remembers the blood on the floor. / Shatter the brittle, temper the keen, / For death is the sharpest tool ever seen."

title: The Brimstone Hound's Muzzle
text: "Iron muzzles for hell hounds must be forged without seams. If the beast's saliva touches raw lead, it dissolves into green smoke. Feed them scrap iron dipped in pig blood to keep their teeth sharp and their temper ferocious."

title: Lava Bridge Maintenance Protocol
text: "Inspect the iron turnbuckles every dawn. The heat causes the chains to stretch three inches each month. If a chain snaps while a supply cart is on the bridge, do not reach for the driver—jump for the southern ledge and commend your soul to the stone."

title: The Obsidian Heart
text: "A warrior who swallows a fragment of polished volcanic glass will feel his blood boil for seven days. If his heart does not burst from the pressure, his muscles will harden like cooled basalt, capable of deflecting blows that would fell an ox."

title: The Smelter's Cough
text: "After ten years in the lower foundry, a man does not cough phlegm; he coughs black soot and glittering iron dust. When he dies, his lungs do not rot—they are sold to the blacksmiths as high-grade polishing sponges."

title: Farewell Letter from Foreman Dirk
text: "The magma rose two feet higher during the night shift. The sluice gates are warped shut. Ignis refuses to blow the blast vents because it would ruin the temper on his giant sword. Tell my wife I left the silver under the hearthstone. The heat is coming through the floorboards now."

title: The Astrologer's Madness
text: "The stars on the ceiling of the crypt are not dead stones. They are eyes. Billions of unblinking pupils that pulse in synchrony with our heartbeat. Yesterday, one of them blinked back at me. I wrote down its coordinates in blood from my nose. Now I can hear it scratching at the ceiling tiles above my bed."

title: Principles of Astral Mirroring
text: "An astral mirror reflects not what is, but what ought to be. When an enemy casts a projectile through your mirrored ward, they are striking at their own future corpse. The spell merely fulfills the timeline by returning to its origin with doubled velocity."

title: The Anatomy of a Mimic
text: "A book mimic does not use teeth of bone; its pages are sharpened vellum coated in a fast-acting paralytic enzyme. When you reach to turn the page, the book snaps shut, severing your fingers and absorbing your ink and blood directly into its marginalia."

title: Chronos and the Stolen Seconds
text: "Where do the seconds go when an hourglass runs empty? Chronos collects them in crystal phials. He drinks the childhood of kings and the final moments of dying soldiers like vintage wine. In his library, yesterday is tomorrow, and your grave is already open."

title: The Scribe's Bleeding Hands
text: "I have copied the Grand Grimoire forty times. Each time, the letters shift when the ink dries. Words of praise become instructions for human sacrifice; recipes for bread turn into rituals for summoning insect swarms. The ink has its own will, and it hates the white paper."

title: Void Displacement Theory
text: "Space is not a solid canvas; it is a loosely woven carpet full of holes. To evade an oncoming spear, one need not leap aside. One need only step into the threadbare gap between seconds and re-emerge two paces behind the thrust."

title: Catalogue of Forbidden Shelves
text: "Shelf 44-B: Do not read aloud, or your tongue will split like a serpent's. Shelf 44-C: Contains books bound in the skin of drowned babies; handles with silver tongs only. Shelf 44-D: Empty, yet weighs three hundred pounds. The air around it smells of ozone and dead carnations."

title: The Gargoyle's Vigil
text: "They are not stone carved by human hands. They are wizards who cast a silence ward so powerful it froze their own blood into granite. Now they sit upon the library rafters, waiting for someone to chant a spell so they may dive down and shatter the blasphemy."

title: The Living Inscription
text: "Read the words upon the marble archway backward while holding a black candle in your left palm. The letters will crawl off the stone and burrow beneath your fingernails, leaving permanent blue runes that channel the ambient mana of the dungeon."

title: Malazar's Golden Mask
text: "Behind the polished silver mask of Grand Archivist Malazar, there is no face. There is only a swirling vortex of shredded manuscript scraps fluttering in a perpetual draft. When he speaks, it sounds like thousands of dry pages turning in an abandoned house."

title: The Tome of Endless Hallways
text: "I opened page 14 and stepped through the margin. I have walked for three days between two lines of text. The sentences are walls of solid basalt fifty cubits high. The punctuation marks are pits of bubbling tar. I cannot find the back cover."

title: The Memory Eater's Appetite
text: "First, it takes your mother's name. You do not notice the loss; you simply feel a mild breeze pass through your skull. Next, it takes the memory of fire, so when your hand burns on the brazier, you only stare in wonder at the smell of roasting meat. Finally, it takes your name."

title: Runic Script of the Nethermancers
text: "The glyph of destruction must be inscribed with a diamond stylus dipped in viper venom. When drawn with absolute geometric symmetry, it vibrates at a frequency that fractures the crystalline lattice of enemy shields."

title: A Warning to Curious Scholars
text: "If you hear weeping from inside a hollow volume, do not pry open the clasp. It is the unfinished draft of a dead poet who realized that beauty cannot save him from the worms. His grief is contagious; three scholars have hanged themselves from the spiral staircase after reading his second sonnet."

title: The Astrolabe of Broken Constellations
text: "The brass rings do not track the sun or moon. They track the slow convergence of seven outer terrors whose bodies are larger than whole solar systems. The smallest ring just clicked into place. We have less time than the church claims."

title: Discipline of the Mind Bastion
text: "When confronted by psychic horrors, visualize your consciousness as a granite fortress with narrow arrow slits and iron portcullises. Let the alien thoughts break against the stone like winter waves against a cliffside."

title: The Ink Horror's Lifecycle
text: "When ten thousand lies are written in the dark, the ink upon the parchment gains sentience. It drips from the books like black honey, gathering into puddles that crawl across the marble. It seeks out open mouths, eager to drown the living in ancient falsehoods."

title: The Echo of the Unwritten
text: "You will meet yourself in the eastern reading room. He will be holding your weapons and wearing your face, but his eyes will be blank white paper. He knows every strike you have practiced since childhood, for he was born of your self-doubt."

title: Preservation of Arcane Vellum
text: "Rub the leather covers with cedar oil and ground dragon scales to protect against moisture and rot. Armor treated with this concoction turns glossy as beetle wings and shrugs off corrosive arcane acid."

title: The Last Entry in the Grand Index
text: "Book #999,999: Title: The Reader. Synopsis: A miserable fool standing in the dark with a lantern, reading about his own doom while the creature behind him silently raises its claws. (Do not turn around)."

title: The Blood-Tree's Thirst
text: "The weeping oaks of the Kurgan do not drink rain. Their roots reach deep into the mass graves of the third heresy, drawing up gallons of clotted blood to nourish their swollen black acorns. If you carve into their bark, they bleed warm crimson sap that smells of iron and fever."

title: Hymn to the Antlered Lord
text: "He who runs with the stag must shed his human skin! / The forest demands bone for bone, blood for leaf. / Strike with the fury of the rutting elk; / Let your horns tear the sky and your hooves crush the weak into soft loam."

title: Lady Isolde's Wedding Gift
text: "Her husband gave her a pearl necklace with twelve matching gems. On their wedding night, she discovered the pearls were the dried eggs of subterranean corpse-spiders. By morning, the eggs had hatched into her throat. Now she sings with eight voices from within her silk bower."

title: The Bramble's Snare
text: "The thorns of the blighted forest have backwards-facing barbs like fishing hooks. When caught in a snare, struggling only drives the barbs deeper into muscle tissue. Breathe slowly, flex the limb in the direction of the vine's curve, and slide free like an eel through marsh grass."

title: The Barrow Hag's Stew
text: "Throw in three hemlock roots dug by midnight, the gall bladder of a black bear, and the wedding band of an unfaithful widow. Simmer over peat smoke until the grease forms faces upon the surface. Drink it, and you will see the ghosts of everyone you have ever wronged, pointing and laughing."

title: Anatomy of the Rotwood Treant
text: "It is not wood, but calcified bone and petrified fungi woven into the shape of a tree. Its heartwood contains a screaming corpse encased in resin sixty years ago. To kill it, do not bring fire—it will only become a walking conflagration. Bring axes of cold iron and sever the taproot."

title: The Crimson Dolmen
text: "The ancient megaliths were dragged from the mountains before men learned to forge iron. Lie naked upon the central stone during the eclipse, allowing the cold stone to leech the weakness from your spine. You will rise with bones like black oak."

title: The Screaming Larvae
text: "They hatch in the puddles of stagnant blood left after battle. Smaller than a thumb, with faces resembling distorted infants. They screech when stepped upon, and their screech draws every bloodhound within three miles. Crush them with your heel and do not look back."

title: Diary of a Lost Woodsman
text: "The trees moved while I slept. I left my blazing axe marks on the trunk of the weeping ash, but when I woke, the marks were gone and the branches had woven themselves into an arch above my bedroll. The ground is breathing beneath my boots."

title: The Cannibal's Covenant
text: "The marrow of the beast gives strength to the arm, but the marrow of your fellow warrior gives cunning to the mind. Wash your hands in the cold brook, slice thin along the rib, and remember that survival is the only morality recognized by the wolves."

title: The Will-o'-the-Blight's Dance
text: "Do not follow the pale blue flame through the peat moss. It is not the lantern of a lost traveler; it is the burning methane of three hundred corpses decomposing beneath the sod. Step where the light leads, and the ground will open its wet mouth to swallow you whole."

title: The Stag Skull Helmet
text: "Carved from an eight-point elk that drowned in the blood well. The bone has absorbed the iron of a hundred sacrifices. Wear it, and the trees will bow as you pass, but you will never taste cooked meat again—your mouth will water only for bitter moss and salt licks."

title: Curse of the Withered Crop
text: "The wheat in the border valley grew tall and golden, but when the farmers ground the kernels between stones, black blood oozed from the flour. The bread smelled of burnt tallow. Those who ate of it gave birth to children with hands like thorn branches."

title: Secrets of the Barrow Snipers
text: "A bone javelin must be carved from the tibia of a predator and feathered with crow quills dipped in adder poison. Release the string upon the exhalation, aiming for the hollow behind the collarbone where the heart-vessel thrums."

title: The Weeping Dolmen of Karr
text: "Every winter solstice, the standing stone of Karr sheds clear tears that smell of lilacs. If caught in a crystal vial, the water heals blindness, but causes the patient to see the world as a decaying charnel house crawling with transparent worms."

title: The Spider-Silk Shroud
text: "Lady Isolde's maids spin thread not from flax, but from the silk glands of subterranean widow-beasts. The resulting fabric is lighter than breath and stronger than iron wire. A shirt woven of this silk will turn a sword thrust, but slowly burrow into your ribs like living wires."

title: The Graverobber's Stake
text: "When digging into an ancient kurgan mound, drive an ash-wood stake through the turf before striking with the shovel. If the stake bleeds, fill the hole immediately and run. The chieftain inside has not finished rotting."

title: The Totem of Living Bone
text: "Splice the jawbones of wolves into the rib cages of bears, binding them with copper wire and wet sinew. Stand the totem at the threshold of your camp. The spirits of the wild will recognize the sovereign geometry of predation and turn away."

title: Lament of the Blighted Queen
text: "I had castles of white limestone and gardens of pale roses. Now I have only roots that crawl through my eye sockets and spiders that whisper of treason in the dark. Come closer, sweet champion. Let me wrap you in my cold, sticky embrace."

title: The Final Hunt
text: "When the horn of Cernunnos blows through the midnight forest, every beast lays its ears flat and trembles in its den. The quarry of the wild hunt is never the deer or the boar; it is the last scrap of human mercy left in the heart of the wanderer."

title: Genesis of the Hollow Sovereign
text: "Before the five dungeons were partitioned, there stood a single empire whose towers pierced the clouds. But its emperor feared the silent rot of age. He dug into the primeval mantle, unearthing the Five Seals of the Void. In breaking them, he divided his kingdom into five eternal prisons, crowning himself ruler of nothingness."

title: The Merchant's Secret Ledger
text: "Archibald and Malphas are not two distinct souls; they are the left and right hands of the same ancient collector. Archibald takes the gilded toys of your vanity; Malphas takes the vital essence of your beating heart. Both smile as you walk toward the boss chamber, knowing you will not return."

title: The Mystery of the Gilded Keys
text: "Why does the golden key appear on only half the floors? It is not chance. The key is drawn to the smell of despair. It manifests only when a soul in the party has contemplated abandoning their companions. The key does not unlock salvation; it unlocks an opportunity to spend your gold before you die."

title: The Five Seals of the Chasm
text: "Study the geometry of the five dungeon levels: The Crypt of Bone, the Sewers of Rot, the Foundry of Slag, the Archives of Ink, and the Kurgan of Blood. They are not random caverns. They are the five internal organs of a dead god, suspended in eternal putrefaction beneath the surface of the world."

title: Tome of Forbidden Apotheosis
effect_text: +1 Skill Point & +5 Stat Points (Permanent Free Allocation)
text: "Before the dawn of light and shadow, there was only the Unshaped Will. Gaze into this abyssal vellum, mortal, and take the chisel of creation into your trembling hands. Rewrite the fundamental architecture of your soul. Distribute five drops of divine potency among your faculties, and unlock the secret art of your chosen lineage. No deity has the courage to stay your hand."
